newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leaders of Israel, Jordan meet in secret - paper.
newsitem.headline: Leaders of Israel, Jordan meet in secret - paper.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein met secretly in Jordan late at night to try to patch up a row over water, the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth said on Friday.
The daily, Israel's biggest, said Netanyahu and King Hussein also discussed reviving Israeli-Palestinian peace talks stalled for two months. The king has in the past played a broker's role.
It said Netanyahu flew by a military helicopter with close advisers and high-ranking army officers to the summit at Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.
Israel Radio said former general Ariel Sharon, who as national infrastructure minister is responsible for water in Israel, also took part, meeting the Jordanian monarch for the first time.
It was not immediately clear if any progress was made to resolve the water crisis.

Netanyahu's office would neither confirm nor deny a meeting took place. A spokeswoman declined comment when asked by Reuters why a summit meeting between two countries at peace for nearly three years had to be secret at all.
"We aren't relating to it," she said of the report.
There was no immediate comment from Jordan.
Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan cancelled a meeting on Tuesday with Netanyahu because of disagreements over water supplies promised to the Arab kingdom under their 1994 peace treaty.
Jordanian officials had accused Israel of backing out at the last minute from an accord to help the kingdom, facing growing water shortages, find an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year.
The treaty, ending a 46-year state of war, specified that within a year of its coming into force in November 1994 the two sides would develop a plan to supply Jordan with the water.
Ideas for the water supply included desalination plants, dam building, and steps to ease pollution of river waters. But no plan was formally implemented.

Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh spoke this week of a "frustration in the whole peace process" among Jordanians, and said Israel's failure to follow up its commitment to help find water supplies for Jordan was a breach of the 1994 treaty.

In Jerusalem and the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip on Thursday, U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross appeared to be making little progress in his latest mission to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations.
"I cannot tell you that I am optimistic," Netanyahu told reporters in Israel on Thursday evening.

Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down two months ago after Netanyahu gave the final go-ahead for the construction of 6,500 houses for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem on land occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Ross, on his second mission in a month, met Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Gaza and Netanyahu in Jerusalem. Ross was due to meet Arafat again later on Friday in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
